hints: Look carefully at the two ends of molecule M and the middle group, what three oxygen-containing functional groups can you spot?
Remember that excess LiAlH4 is a very strong reducing agent, it reduces both carboxylic acids and aldehydes all the way to alcohols.
First work out the formula of M as C5H8O4, then track how many O atoms are lost and how many H atoms are gained when COOH becomes CH2OH and CHO becomes CH2OH.
walkthrough:
**Work out the structure and formula of M**

Start by expanding the skeletal formula. Reading left to right it is HOOC-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-CHO.

Count the atoms: 5 C, 4 O (2 in acid, 1 in alcohol, 1 in aldehyde) and 8 H. So:
$$M = \text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_4$$

**Recall what LiAlH4 does**

LiAlH4 reduces carbonyl compounds, but it leaves C-OH alcohol groups alone.

Key rules: $\text{RCOOH} \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$. Dilute acid is just added at the end to protonate the alkoxide ions to alcohols.

**Apply reduction to both ends of M**

The left carboxylic acid $\text{-COOH}$ becomes a primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. The right aldehyde $\text{-CHO}$ also becomes a primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. The middle secondary alcohol $\text{-CH(OH)-}$ is unchanged.

Final product is therefore:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Count the formula of the triol product**

Now count again. Carbons are still 5. Oxygens are now 3, one for each OH group.

Hydrogens: $3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 12$. So the molecular formula is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_3$.

options.A: C5H6O5 is incorrect. It has more O and fewer H than the starting material, which is impossible for a reduction. Reduction with LiAlH4 removes O and adds H, it never adds O.
options.B: C5H10O4 is incorrect. This keeps 4 oxygens, suggesting one carbonyl was not reduced. In fact with excess LiAlH4 both the carboxylic acid and the aldehyde are fully reduced to primary alcohols, so one O atom is lost as water.
options.C: C5H10O3 is incorrect. This has the right number of O atoms (3) but too few H atoms. It is the trap for confusing LiAlH4 with NaBH4, which would reduce only the aldehyde and leave the carboxylic acid unchanged, or for miscounting the H gain.
options.D: C5H12O3 is correct. Both reducible groups are reduced: COOH to CH2OH (gain 2 H, lose 1 O) and CHO to CH2OH (gain 2 H). Starting from C5H8O4 this gives C5H12O3, a triol HOCH2CH2CH(OH)CH2CH2OH.
